Title: 'Trump has cost us': After midterm losses, MAGA asks if it's over
Article:
DALLAS: As Republicans faced a nationwide drubbing in Tuesday's midterm elections, supporters streamed out of a Dallas ballroom where they had hoped to toast a win for US Senate candidate Ken Paxton, a favourite of President Donald Trump.
In the hotel bar, Michael Little, a 59-year-old businessman and three-time Trump voter, stared at the president's image on a television screen.
"People are pissed off at Trump. Trump has cost us," he said, capturing a sentiment rippling through the president's Make America Great Again movement after the Republican Party's worst electoral defeat in decades.
Across the coalition, some supporters who once viewed Trump as MAGA's greatest asset are beginning to question whether he has become its biggest liability.
Still, the midterm losses amounted to more than a repudiation of Trump. They were a referendum on the political and cultural movement he built.
A defining force in American politics that began as a campaign slogan during Trump's 2016 presidential run now faces a potentially existential reckoning after voters disillusioned with soaring fuel prices, the Iran war and corruption in Washington delivered Democrats decisive congressional majorities.
Trump's first major response to the midterms came on Friday. Instead of changing course, he doubled down on the movement's core. He promoted Stephen Miller, the main architect of the administration's hardline immigration crackdown, to chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles. Wiles was seen as a stabilising force inside an often chaotic White House.
The move was celebrated by some of MAGA's most ardent influencers, who saw it as a return to the anti-immigration agenda at the movement's roots. "Exactly the energy we need," right-wing influencer Benny Johnson posted on X to his 4.1 million followers. "Solid move. It's Miller Time."
The White House did not directly answer Reuters' questions about why Republicans lost, the defeat of candidates who embraced Trump's false 2020 election claims, or where MAGA goes from here. Instead, it pointed to Trump's remarks on Wednesday, when he said, "If I were on the ballot, we would have won." He also said it was "largely true" that the Iran war had cost Republicans because "it drove the gasoline up", but that he would do it again.
For nearly a decade, MAGA has reshaped the Republican Party and transformed national debates on issues such as trade, immigration, race and gender.
The movement installed loyalists throughout federal agencies, cracked down on immigration and pressured corporations and public institutions to retreat from diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives.
MAGA survived the fallout from the Jan 6, 2021, attack on the US Capitol and propelled Trump back to the White House. Now, the Democrats' sweeping victory has forced the movement to grapple with an unexpected question: Is MAGA over?
Reuters interviews with more than a dozen MAGA activists, influencers, party strategists, Christian nationalist leaders and researchers who track right-wing politics, along with a review of MAGA supporters' posts and podcasts since Tuesday, show a movement turning its anger on itself.
The stolen-election claims that have driven MAGA since Democrat Joe Biden beat Trump in the 2020 presidential election have mostly gone quiet.
Instead, supporters are blaming Republican leaders and Trump's advisers, and in some cases the president himself, for broken promises on living costs, the Iran war and the government's decision to redact or withhold major portions of its investigative files on late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
MAGA's factions also disagree about what comes next. Some want a return to populist and nationalist basics. Some want a movement less tied to one man. And a vocal minority say MAGA is already dead.
"We have to rebuild," Steve Bannon, a prominent MAGA proponent, podcaster and former Trump White House adviser, told Reuters. He urged the party to double down on an aggressive populist and nationalist agenda and praised Trump for elevating Miller.
"Miller's appointment as chief of staff underpins my point," he said. "There is no more hardcore MAGA proponent than Stephen."
As pro-Trump internet forums digested the election results, a notable slice of self-described MAGA loyalists — more than 20 per cent — raised doubts about the movement's leadership and direction, according to an analysis of social media traffic done for Reuters by PeakMetrics, a data intelligence firm.
About half of that cohort remained supportive of the MAGA movement but no longer backed Trump as its leader. The other half remained loyal to, though critical of, the president himself.
The analysis was based on 12,850 posts sampled from a universe of 4.6 million Trump-related comments on X and Reddit from 9pm on Election Day to 8pm the next evening. It found broad concern among MAGA supporters as the results became clear.
Of the posts that assigned blame for the rout, nearly a third said concerns about the Iran war and Israel's influence over US policy had overshadowed Trump's message. A quarter said Republicans not fully committed to the MAGA agenda had undermined the movement.
The results left Trump facing large Democratic majorities in both chambers of Congress. In the Senate, Democrats could control as many as 56 of the chamber's 100 seats, more than enough to block Trump's future judicial picks.
Republicans might not be able to recapture the Senate until 2032, Republican Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said the morning after the election.
"It's the political equivalent of a meteor strike that went all around the United States," DeSantis said at a post-election briefing.
Democrats will now control governorships in seven battleground states Trump won in 2024 and, strikingly, they won every statewide race in Texas, which has not backed a Democratic presidential candidate since 1976.
[[nid:1573476]]
MAGA is stale
Since Tuesday, talk of election fraud has virtually vanished among right-wing influencers.
"I have been banging the drum of rigged and stolen elections since 2020, but that is not why we lost the midterms," Rogan O'Handley, a MAGA influencer who posts under the name DC_Draino, wrote on X to his 2.3 million followers.
"We lost because we failed to fix the things voters sent us to do." He did not respond to a request for comment.
After the 2020 election, Trump supporter Isabella DeLuca was among thousands who stormed the US Capitol on Jan 6, 2021. She was charged with five crimes, including theft of a table from inside the Capitol, and pleaded not guilty. Her case was dismissed after Trump returned to office and pardoned her.
This time, the 26-year-old conservative influencer directed her anger towards what she described as out-of-touch Republican leaders who failed to appeal to Gen Z voters on affordability, avoiding foreign wars and other key issues.
"Republicans were just lazy. They felt like that they were entitled to people's votes and that people would vote for them no matter what," DeLuca told Reuters. "It goes to show you that you do have to earn people's votes, and that even in a super red state like Texas, you're not untouchable."
The MAGA movement this year appeared "tired", she said.
That sentiment was echoed in online right-wing forums, said Jennifer Golbeck, a University of Maryland professor who has analysed MAGA-related posts since 2016. She said engagement by Trump's most loyal backers has steadily declined since January, including a 27 per cent drop in posts and comments on Patriots.Win, a popular MAGA forum.
"The enthusiasm and the passion even among this hardest core group of supporters hasn't really been there," Golbeck said. "They are saying that 'MAGA is stale.' It's not new and exciting like it once was."
Fox News, a cable network that has long been a key platform for MAGA voices, saw a sharp decline in viewership ahead of the midterms, with its total daytime audience down 27 per cent in October from a year earlier, according to Nielsen, the audience measurement firm.
In a statement to Reuters, Fox said it drew more viewers than its cable-news rivals on election night. "FOX News has been the number one network in cable news for a quarter century," spokesperson Caley Cronin said.
Some prominent right-wing influencers blamed the president's advisers or Republican lawmakers — but rarely Trump himself — for ignoring key voter concerns. In posts, online broadcasts and interviews with Reuters, many blamed dissatisfaction with the economy, though they differed on other reasons for Tuesday's results.
It wasn't just failure to address affordability that "crushed" Republicans, said Ben Shapiro, co-founder of the conservative site Daily Wire, on his online show on Wednesday. "If you're talking about an electoral catastrophe — a wipeout like we saw last night — you need more ingredients. Here are the other ingredients: chaos and corruption."
Laura Loomer, an influencer close to Trump, wrote on X: "America is over and the American Dream is dead." Yet she told Reuters the losses did not signal the end of MAGA, arguing that anyone seeking the 2028 Republican presidential nomination would need Trump's base.
"The Republican Party belongs to President Trump," Loomer said. "The MAGA movement is still the majority of the GOP base, and whoever wants to run for president in 2028 on the GOP ticket, they would be unwise to be dismissive of President Trump."
On Thursday, Loomer put her podcast on hiatus, saying she had been "running on empty for too long" and needed to focus on her personal life and upcoming wedding. She would return in January, she added.
[[nid:1573475]]
Broken promises
The midterms also tested the beliefs that have held MAGA together, and some of them are giving way.
The Democratic sweep dealt a significant setback to the election denial movement, a central pillar of MAGA politics since Trump's 2020 defeat. Candidates who embraced his false claims of widespread voter fraud lost heavily, including several who had worked to overturn the 2020 result.
Election deniers will hold at least 41 fewer congressional and statewide offices next year, and they have lost 70 per cent of the called races for statewide posts that oversee elections, according to States United Action, a non-profit that tracks such candidates.
Trump made no effort to contest the results and instead blamed Republicans for the defeat.
With few close races and no credible basis for a challenge, many prominent pro-Trump election sceptics dropped fraud allegations and urged supporters to keep organising. A handful of allies still alleged, without evidence, that the vote was rigged.
Mike Lindell, the MyPillow founder and promoter of false claims that machines flipped votes in 2020, said he was not concerned by Trump's pledge to accept the results. "That's his opinion. I've got a different opinion," Lindell told Reuters. "I think it's all been stolen."
But such claims stayed largely on the fringe, even among Republicans. Without contested races, the MAGA election denial movement risks losing the money, attention and momentum that sustained it. "Nobody's going to be putting money behind it," said Wendy Via, co-founder of the Global Project Against Hate and Extremism, a non-profit that tracks hate speech and extremism.
Retired Lieutenant General Mike Flynn, who falsely claimed the 2020 election was stolen and is a popular figure in the Christian nationalist wing of the MAGA movement, accepted the defeat. He called the results "a massacre" and criticised Trump and his administration for failing to deliver on pledges ranging from lowering costs to releasing the government's investigative files on Epstein.
Responding to Vice President JD Vance's assessment on X that the Iran war was "the reason we lost", Flynn wrote: "the sheer number of broken promises is why the blue tsunami happened."
Flynn also criticised Christian voters for failing to show up. "As a Catholic and a Christian, I'm sorely embarrassed and disappointed," he wrote.
Other prominent Christian nationalists were divided over whether MAGA can outlast Trump.
Douglas Wilson, a Christian nationalist pastor who was invited by US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to deliver a sermon at the Pentagon in February, told Reuters that MAGA "is not going anywhere" but must become less personality-driven and more focused on border control, tax cuts and avoiding foreign wars.
Joel Webbon, a far-right Christian nationalist pastor from Texas, was far less sanguine. "Trump lost this all by himself," he said in a video on X, arguing that the president abandoned his base by embracing Israel, launching the war in Iran and failing to follow through on releasing the Epstein files and mass deportations.
"MAGA is dead," Webbon wrote in an accompanying post. "Forever."

Title: Deepavali brings university breakthrough for orphaned son after mother's 16-year sacrifice
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: A single mother's 16-year sacrifice has culminated in a heartwarming Deepavali milestone, with her orphaned son finally securing a place at university after an appeal overturned a missed admission deadline.
Dayvesh, who lost his father when he was two, grew up watching his mother work tirelessly to support their family while caring for his 84-year-old grandfather, Tata.
By day, she scrubbed floors as a clinic cleaner.
By dusk, she scoured the streets collecting cardboard boxes and scrap items to recycle — tucking away every single sen into a savings tin, held together by one enduring wish: to see her boy step through the doors of a tertiary institution.
That dream nearly slipped away a few months ago when Dayvesh's mobile phone broke down. By the time it was repaired, he discovered an overdue university offer letter in his inbox, but the acceptance deadline had passed.
Desperate to salvage the opportunity, his mother approached Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister and Bukit Mertajam member of parliament Steven Sim for help.
"She did not come to ask for money. She came carrying a dream that had almost shattered," Sim shared in a Facebook post.
"Imagine a mother's heartbreak when a dream years in the making, just an inch away, suddenly slips before her eyes. I immediately sent an appeal letter to the university," he said.
The university accepted the appeal, allowing Dayvesh to take up his place and fulfilling the dream his mother had worked towards for more than a decade.
In the spirit of Deepavali, a multiracial group of youths mentored by Sim also surprised Dayvesh, his mother and Tata with a pre-festival shopping trip.
Sim said he was touched to learn that the youths had raised the money themselves by running community charity stalls, rather than asking him to fund the initiative.
For Tata, it was the first time in years that he had the chance to wear new clothes for the celebration.
The youths later gathered at the family's home for an impromptu party to celebrate Dayvesh's university admission, with Sim making an unannounced visit to join them.
"My heart melted seeing these youths. This is the Malaysia I dreamed of," Sim said, as laughter and warmth filled the modest home.
"My heart melted seeing these youths. This is the Malaysia I dreamed of," he said.
During the gathering, Dayvesh's mother reminded Sim that he had personally delivered a laptop to their home during the Covid-19 lockdowns six years ago, allowing her son to continue his studies.
It was the same laptop Dayvesh had used to work towards his university admission.
Moved by the family's resilience, one of the youths, Zulaikha, then asked to adopt Dayvesh as their younger brother, forging a new bond across cultures.
"These youths did not wait to become wealthy to serve. They only possess one thing: hearts that empathise with the pain of others.
"Our fortune is not what we keep, but what we manage to share. May the light of goodness always illuminate our path forward," Sim said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: MIC calls on Indian voters outside Melaka to return home
Article:
MELAKA: State MIC has called on members of the Indian community living outside Melaka to return home to vote in the state election on Nov 14.
Its chairman, Datuk V.P. Shanmugam, said every vote was important in determining the state's leadership and development direction over the next five years.
He expressed confidence that the Indian community understood the importance of exercising its voting rights and would return to Melaka to cast their ballots.
"As Malaysians, I believe it is our responsibility to make the effort to vote. If we do not turn up, we will be the ones who lose out.
"I believe the Indian community understands how important every vote is under the current circumstances. They will return and vote," he told reporters at a Deepavali open house at his residence in Batu Berendam here today.
Shanmugam was responding to concerns that some of the 40,000 Indian voters in Melaka might not return to vote after celebrating Deepavali.
"As a leader of the Indian community, I have to call on everyone in the community to vote.
"If we fail to vote, we fail to exercise our rights as citizens to choose our leaders," he said.
Separately, Shanmugam welcomed the allocation of a special fund for non-Muslim houses of worship under the joint Barisan Nasional-Perikatan Nasional manifesto unveiled last Friday.
He said the proposal was expected to help address maintenance and development needs at religious facilities, including temples and Chinese temples, in the state.
"As far as benefits for the Indian community are concerned, I believe the manifesto presented by the chief minister has introduced something new, namely funding for non-Muslim houses of worship.
"This means the chief minister may include some allocation for temples and Chinese temples in the budget to be announced soon," he said.
He said assistance for houses of worship had previously also been channelled through allocations provided by the respective elected representatives.
He hoped the dedicated fund would help address the various needs of houses of worship in a more systematic manner.
MIC is fielding one candidate, S. Nadarajah, to defend the Gadek state seat in the Melaka election. The seat was previously held by Shanmugam.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 102 Melaka locations at risk of flooding during spring tides until Nov 17
Article:
KOTA MELAKA: A total of 102 locations in Melaka have been identified as flood-risk areas following the spring tide phenomenon, which is expected to continue until Nov 17.
Caretaker Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh called on residents, particularly those living in coastal areas, to remain vigilant over the risk of flash floods during the period.
A spring tide is a tide with an unusually high high-water mark and low low-water mark. This occurs around the new and full moons when the sun, Earth and moon line up and their gravitational pulls combine.
He said preparations included round-the-clock flood monitoring across six main river basins, as well as continuous recording of rainfall and river water levels.
"The early warning system is also being strengthened with the installation of 14 flood warning sirens and 10 monitoring cameras at strategic locations throughout Melaka," he said.
Rauf said this at a campaign programme for the 16th Melaka election at the Barisan Nasional operations room in Kota Laksamana.
Rauf, who is also State BN chairman, said the 102 locations were identified based on records showing flooding at least three times in the past three years.
He said the state government had also provided various flood control assets, including 21 water control gates, 21 pump houses and 14 portable emergency pumps for deployment in critical areas.
Flood mitigation infrastructure was also being monitored, including 105 flood retention ponds and maintenance work in high-risk river basins.
In a related development, Rauf said 447 minor works costing RM40.38 million had been carried out this year to further reduce flood risks in the state.
"These measures reflect the state government's continued commitment to strengthening flood management infrastructure, improving preparedness for disasters and reducing risks to the safety and well-being of the people.
"Through the Disaster Management Committee, the Melaka government will keep issuing announcements from time to time so that early warnings can be given and emergency response can be carried out effectively.
"The public, especially residents in flood-risk areas, are advised to remain vigilant and get the latest information through the Melaka government's official channels," he said.

Title: 195 underage patrons detained in raid on unlicensed Kuala Lumpur nightclub
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police detained 195 underage patrons and a premises manager during a raid on an unlicensed entertainment outlet in the capital shortly after midnight yesterday.
Dang Wangi police chief assistant commissioner Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said those detained comprised 93 local males, 61 local females, 16 foreign males and 25 foreign females.
He said 16 outlet workers and 219 other patrons were also checked.
Investigations found that the outlet was operating without a licence and had allowed underage patrons to enter.
"The premises manager is being investigated under Section 29(2) of the Entertainment (Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur) Regulations for allowing underage patrons into the entertainment premises.
"All those detained, aged between 18 and 64, were taken to the Dang Wangi District Police Headquarters for summonses, documentation and further investigation," he said in a statement.
Azwan said checks found that none of the individuals inspected had any outstanding criminal records, while preliminary urine screening found an adult male patron positive for amphetamine and methamphetamine.
"Enforcement action will continue to be intensified to curb any illegal activities," he said.
He also urged members of the public with information on criminal activities to channel it through the Kuala Lumpur Police Hotline at 03-2146 0522 / 03-2146 0585, the Dang Wangi District Police Control Centre at 03-2600 2222 or any nearby police station.

Title: Malaysia eyes satellite connectivity to strengthen disaster communications, says Fahmi
Article:
DOHA: Malaysia is looking to leverage satellite connectivity and artificial intelligence (AI) to strengthen disaster preparedness and ensure communications remain available during emergencies, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said emerging technologies could complement conventional telecommunications infrastructure, particularly in remote and disaster-affected areas where alternative connectivity solutions might be required.
He said Malaysia also saw potential in integrating terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks to strengthen communications resilience during emergencies.
"Looking ahead, Malaysia sees opportunities to further leverage emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, satellite connectivity and integrated terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks, to strengthen disaster preparedness and communications resilience.
"These technologies can complement conventional infrastructure, particularly in remote or disaster-affected areas where alternative connectivity solutions may be required," he said.
Fahmi was speaking at the Digital Leadership Forum Ministerial Panel held in conjunction with Mobile World Congress (MWC) Doha 2026.
He said Malaysia was placing greater emphasis on strengthening emergency telecommunications capabilities to ensure essential communications remained available when conventional networks were disrupted.
He added that reliable connectivity was crucial during disasters as it enabled emergency response teams to coordinate rescue operations and affected communities to access essential information.
"During a disaster, connectivity is not merely a convenience. It can be the difference between receiving timely assistance and being left isolated," he said.
To address these challenges, Fahmi said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) had developed MCMC Prime, a mobile radio and internet communications system designed to support connectivity when conventional telecommunications networks are disrupted.
He said the system provided an alternative means of communication during emergencies and supported coordination among response teams while maintaining access to essential information.
The initiative was particularly relevant during severe flooding when damaged telecommunications infrastructure or disrupted electricity supply could affect conventional mobile networks, he added.
Fahmi said Malaysia's approach also emphasised close coordination between MCMC and telecommunications operators, as well as the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) and other authorities.
He said such cooperation was essential to support disaster preparedness and identify affected network infrastructure while coordinating restoration efforts and facilitating communications for emergency responders and affected communities.
He said timely public warnings and reliable access to official information would enable communities to take appropriate precautionary measures during emergencies.
"Network resilience is not simply about preventing infrastructure failure. It is about ensuring that essential communications can continue, or be restored as quickly as possible, when lives and public safety are at stake," he said.

Title: YNH Property races to plug RM6.8mil sukuk reserve gap
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: YNH Property Bhd is working to plug a RM6.8 million shortfall in its sukuk reserve account as it steps up efforts to meet a RM170 million Islamic debt maturity due on Feb 26 next year.
The property developer said it had accumulated RM54.4 million in the designated reserve account as at Oct 27, against the required balance of RM61.2 million for October.
YNH Property said the difference arose from the scheduled accumulation of funds under the sukuk Wakalah arrangement and did not represent a missed principal repayment.
It is taking steps to meet the required balance within the stipulated contractual remedy period.
The funding challenge comes after MARC Ratings downgraded the group's RM700 million Islamic medium-term notes programme and placed the rating on MARCWatch Negative.
YNH Property said its immediate priorities were meeting monthly reserve-account requirements, accelerating collections from ongoing developments and completing asset disposals to fulfil its financial commitments.
A key part of its funding plan is the proposed RM170 million disposal of its Desa Sri Hartamas land to Sunway Living Space Sdn Bhd.
The company is working with the purchaser and advisers to fulfil the remaining conditions precedent.
Upon completion, the transaction is expected to generate about RM105 million in net cash proceeds after settling the RM65 million loan secured against the land, subject to final adjustments and costs.
YNH Property is also relying on construction progress and sales billings at its Solasta Dutamas project in Kuala Lumpur and townships in Manjung, Perak, to generate progressive billings and cash inflows.
Group managing director Allan Yu Kai Leun said the company recognised that market confidence depended on meeting its commitments.
"Our responsibility is to turn project sales and asset monetisation into cash within the required timelines, while keeping our developments moving on the ground.
"The February 2027 sukuk maturity is a clear priority for management. We will communicate our progress through concrete funding and transaction milestones, so that our sukuk holders, bankers, and shareholders can assess our position based on facts," he said in a statement.
Separately, YNH said its audited financial statements for the financial year ended June 30, 2026, published on Oct 30, received an unmodified audit opinion from Morison LC PLT, following qualified opinions in the preceding three reporting periods.
The board also approved the implementation of its Investment Governance Standard Operating Policies and Procedures during the financial year.
YNH Property has more than 324 hectares of undeveloped land, which it views as a longer-term development and monetisation pipeline rather than an immediate source of liquidity.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nations must not fall victim to 'technology colonialism', says Fahmi
Article:
DOHA: Malaysia has called for greater respect for national sovereignty in shaping telecommunications policies and warned against "technology colonialism".
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said every nation must retain the freedom to determine its own technological direction, particularly as geopolitical rivalries and competing technology ecosystems increasingly influence global telecommunications development.
"There should not be a case of a kind of technological colonialism where if you are the first, then you dictate to others what you should or shouldn't do, what you can or cannot do.
"Nations are sovereign and should be able to decide their own domestic policy," he said during a ministerial panel discussion at Mobile World Congress (MWC) Doha 2026.
Technological colonialism is a term where advanced nations dictate how others develop and deploy their digital infrastructure.
Fahmi said Malaysia's experience in rolling out its 5G network demonstrated the importance of maintaining policy independence while navigating complex geopolitical and diplomatic considerations.
He said Malaysia initially adopted a single wholesale network model for its 5G deployment despite recommendations against such an approach by GSMA Intelligence, before transitioning to a dual-network model.
"Malaysia is unique because we did what GSMA Intelligence said not to do: roll out 5G using a single wholesale network. But we did it anyway, and I was the minister in charge of transitioning it into a dual-network model," he said.
Fahmi described the transition as a challenging undertaking that required Malaysia to navigate diplomatic sensitivities while balancing domestic priorities against international technological standards.
He said discussions on digital sovereignty should extend beyond technological self-reliance to encompass the broader principle of national sovereignty.
He added that an increasingly multipolar global environment demands greater dialogue and engagement among countries to find common ground rather than deepen divisions.
"In this increasingly multipolar age, we need to have more conversations, more engagements, and find meeting points rather than things that split us apart," he added.
Fahmi said the principle of interoperability, which enables different telecommunications networks and technologies to function together, would face significant tests as countries pursued their respective digital strategies.
He pointed out that Asean's consensus-based approach presents its own unique dynamics, given the absence of a central parliament and the bloc's strong emphasis on respecting member states' national sovereignty.
As such, he said, building trust and achieving interoperability requires countries to look beyond their national borders and bolster international cooperation.
Fahmi also spoke on the need to assist emerging nations in bridging digital divides, particularly as the telecommunications sector prepares for quantum migration and quantum-safe communications.
He said greater focus should be placed on driving the practical adoption of existing networks before the industry shifts its attention entirely to sixth-generation (6G) technologies.
"Before we talk about 6G, we have to look at who is actually using 5G or 5G-Advanced - that remains a key challenge we are actively addressing in Malaysia," he said.
Despite the hurdles, Fahmi expressed confidence that international collaboration could spur innovative breakthroughs, particularly from nations not traditionally viewed as global technology leaders.
"There are many challenges, but there are also many opportunities for us to discover solutions together, and sometimes you might find those solutions in the unlikeliest of countries," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fahmi highlights Malaysia's early 5G coverage milestone at MWC Doha
Article:
DOHA: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has highlighted Malaysia's progress in expanding its 5G network, with the country's second network achieving 90 per cent coverage in October, nine months ahead of schedule.
He said the achievement marked significant progress in Malaysia's transition to a dual 5G network model aimed at strengthening competition, encouraging investment and improving telecommunications service quality.
Fahmi said Malaysia had also invested significantly in expanding and strengthening its digital infrastructure through the National Digital Network Plan (Jendela) since 2020.
"As of July, approximately 10.12 million premises had been passed by fibre, significantly improving access to high-speed broadband services," he said at the Digital Leadership Forum Ministerial Panel held in conjunction with Mobile World Congress (MWC) Doha 2026.
Fahmi said Malaysia had also made substantial progress in 5G deployment, with the second network achieving 90 per cent coverage nine months ahead of schedule.
He said the development reflected the country's efforts to establish a competitive and sustainable telecommunications ecosystem while ensuring that consumers benefited from improved service quality.
However, Fahmi said Malaysia's digital infrastructure development was not solely focused on expanding network coverage, as service quality, affordability and resilience were equally important.
He said these elements must be addressed together to ensure digital connectivity delivered meaningful benefits to the people.
"Through the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission, or MCMC, we continue to promote infrastructure sharing and efficient network deployment, while addressing connectivity gaps in underserved communities," he said.
Fahmi said the Universal Service Provision (USP) framework also played an important role in extending telecommunications services to areas where commercial investment alone might not be viable.
He said the approach enabled Malaysia to balance infrastructure investment with the need to ensure that telecommunications services remained accessible and affordable.
"For Malaysia, a successful network model is one that combines strong infrastructure, sustainable investment, effective regulation and meaningful access for all," he added.
Fahmi is currently in Doha to lead the Malaysian delegation to the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Plenipotentiary Conference (PP-26), which runs from Nov 6 to 11.
His working visit to Doha also carries the important mission of securing Malaysia's re-election to the ITU Council for the 2027-2030 term.
He is accompanied by Communications Ministry deputy secretary-general (telecommunications infrastructure) Mano Verabathran.
The Malaysian delegation also comprises representatives from the MCMC and local telecommunications industry players, including Telekom Malaysia, CelcomDigi, Maxis and U Mobile.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Japan man with 'grudge against society' stabs bookshop worker
Article:
TOKYO: Japanese police arrested a 33-year-old man who admitted to stabbing a bookshop worker in Osaka on Sunday, a spokesman told AFP, adding that the suspect said he "held a grudge against society".
The man, identified as Satoshi Okamoto, allegedly used a kitchen knife to stab the worker — who called police immediately afterwards — at a branch of national chain Maruzen & Junkudo in the heart of Japan's second-largest city.
Police did not elaborate on the victim's condition, but said there was no fear for his life.
The suspect, who had remained inside the store until his arrest, admitted to the stabbing and told officers, "I held a grudge against society as a whole", according to the police spokesman, who briefed AFP on the customary condition of anonymity.
Violent crime is relatively rare in Japan, but there have been occasional stabbings and attacks in recent years committed by socially isolated individuals airing grievances against the world at large.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KTMB denies ownership of storage facility destroyed in Sepang fire
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) has clarified that the storage facility destroyed in a fire at Desa Pinggiran Putra, Sepang, was not under its control or responsibility.
Instead, KTMB said the facility, which housed equipment and security management assets, was managed and maintained by contractor X-Rail Systems.
"X-Rail Systems is the contractor carrying out the Klang Valley Double Track (KVDT) Electrification Upgrade Project under the Public Works Department and Transport Ministry.
"KTMB hopes the public and media reports will correct the information regarding the ownership and management of the storage facility to avoid confusion," it said in a statement.
It was reported that an
equipment storage facility
believed to belong to KTMB was destroyed in a fire at Desa Pinggiran Putra, Sepang, at 10.42pm yesterday.
An inspection at the scene found that the fire involved 10 containers, six transformers and several gas cylinders.
The fire also engulfed piles of cables and six diesel drums. Firefighting operations ended at 12.50am today.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Migrant boat sinks off Senegal, 21 killed
Article:
DAKAR: A boat carrying migrants sank off northwestern Senegal, killing at least 21 people in the latest tragedy along the dangerous Atlantic route from Africa to Europe, authorities said.
The Senegalese Interior Ministry said in a statement that only one person had been rescued, in addition to the 21 bodies recovered.
It said the death toll was "provisional" as of late Saturday, adding that the search was still under way and the families of victims were being assisted.
Media reports said the boat capsized on Saturday off the Loumpoul dunes in Kebemer department, between Dakar and the northern city of Saint-Louis.
Le Soleil newspaper said most of the victims were from the Leona and Thieppe districts in the same department.
Senegalese authorities said on Saturday that they had intercepted 142 migrants, including women and children, who were aboard a small boat attempting to reach Spain.
Thousands of people from West Africa have died in recent years while trying to reach Europe via the perilous Atlantic route to Spain's Canary Islands.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Continuous rain warning issued for east coast states, Sabah until Wednesday
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued an alert-level continuous rain warning for several areas in Kelantan, Pahang, Sabah and Terengganu until Wednesday.
In a statement, MetMalaysia said the warning covered Tanah Merah, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Kota Baru, Machang, Bachok, Pasir Puteh, Kuala Krai and Jeli in Kelantan.
In Pahang, the affected areas are Kuantan, Pekan and Rompin, while the warning covers the whole of Terengganu.
In Sabah, continuous rain is forecast from tomorrow until Wednesday in Kudat and Sandakan, including Paitan, Telupid, Labuk and Sugut, Sandakan and Kinabatangan.
The public can obtain the latest weather updates through MetMalaysia's official website and social media platforms, as well as its myCuaca mobile application.
For enquiries, the public can contact the MetMalaysia hotline at 1-300-22-1638.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia stands in solidarity with Poland after shooting tragedy, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia stands in solidarity with the people of Poland and extends its condolences to the families of those killed in a shooting in Kraków, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar also expressed sadness over the tragedy, which claimed six lives and left several others injured, while wishing those affected a swift recovery.
He said he was deeply concerned by reports suggesting that the attacker was influenced by far-right extremism.
"This tragedy underscores the need to confront terrorism in all its forms, including the growing threat of violent right-wing extremism. No ideology can justify the murder of innocent people," he said in a Facebook post.
Anwar reaffirmed Malaysia's commitment to working closely with the international community to counter extremism and uphold peace and human dignity.
In the incident on Saturday afternoon, a gunman, reportedly inspired by far-right ideology killed six people, including a Briton, and injured many others in Kraków, Poland's second-largest city.
According to international media reports citing police, the attacker drove into Main Market Square before opening fire at people in the area.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar brings festive cheer to MIC-MIED Deepavali open house
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today attended the Deepavali open house organised by MIC and the Maju Institute of Educational Development (MIED) at Mansion Oncidium Hall in Kota Kemuning.
He was welcomed by MIC president and MIED chairman Tan Sri SA Vigneswaran, adding to the festive atmosphere at the Festival of Lights celebration, which was attended by nearly 3,000 guests from various ethnic backgrounds.
Anwar spent time mingling with guests and dining with several political leaders, including former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob and MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong.
Commenting on the event, Vigneswaran said the celebration showed that Malaysians could live in harmony and share in the joy of festivals throughout the year.
"This proves that celebrations like this are a clear platform for integration among the races. Although there are differences in political backgrounds, events like this can set them aside for the sake of togetherness," he said.
He also expressed hope that Malaysians would maintain their close ties and make them a source of strength as the country moved towards comprehensive progress.
Meanwhile, Wee said the event was not only lively but also reflected the unique diversity of Malaysians in a spirit of goodwill.
"This is truly the spirit of goodwill that has long existed among Malaysians, and it must be preserved for the prosperity of our beloved country," he said.
At the event, Vigneswaran and Wee accompanied Anwar in cutting a cake to mark the highlight of this year's open house celebration.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Najib's family still awaiting update on house arrest, says daughter
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Datuk Seri Najib Razak's family had prepared to welcome him home last Friday, but their hopes were dashed when the former prime minister remained at Kajang Prison.
His daughter, Nooryana Najwa, said the family was disappointed as they had made preparations in anticipation of his return but were still waiting for the authorities to provide an update on the implementation of his house arrest.
"My family is very disappointed. We had made preparations to welcome my father home last Friday.
"Unfortunately, our hopes have yet to materialise. Datuk Seri Najib is still at Kajang Prison, and we are waiting for the latest developments from the authorities," she said.
She was speaking to reporters while helping with the campaign of Barisan Nasional candidate for the Machap Jaya seat at FELDA Tun Ghafar Baba Hutan Percha here today.
Nooryana said she had also visited her father yesterday and that Najib was deeply disappointed with the latest developments concerning the implementation of house arrest.
Despite the situation, she said, her father continued to pray and hope that the appropriate action would be taken soon.
"We managed to meet him yesterday, and he was very disappointed, extremely disappointed.
"However, he continues to pray and hope that the necessary and appropriate action will be taken in the near future," she said.
On the latest developments, Nooryana said the family had yet to receive any new information and was still waiting for further action.
She added that Najib's legal team had made clear its position that action relating to the implementation of house arrest should be expedited.
Meanwhile, Nooryana said that despite his disappointment, Najib continued to encourage his children who were involved in politics to remain committed to BN's campaign throughout the Melaka election.
She said her father wanted them to continue supporting the party despite the various challenges he was facing.
"As a Puteri Umno executive council member and information chief, I will certainly continue to help my party throughout the campaign.
"Despite his disappointment and the various challenges he is facing, he continues to encourage my brother and me, who are active in politics, to keep campaigning and supporting the party.
"My father's encouragement is among the reasons I continue to go to the ground and assist BN's campaign efforts in Melaka ahead of polling day," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Undocumented migrants pay syndicates up to RM15,000 to enter Malaysia
Article:
KOTA BARU: Undocumented migrants smuggled into Malaysia through illegal jetties or sea routes are believed to pay syndicates between RM5,000 and RM15,000 each.
Southeast Brigade General Operations Force commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the fees depended on the migrants' countries of origin and intended destinations.
"Based on cases reported this year, some undocumented migrants paid between RM5,000 and RM15,000 to agents to arrange their journey into Malaysia.
"However, this is not a fixed rate, as the actual amount depends on the route, destination and services provided by the syndicates," he said when contacted.
Radzi said at least seven illegal jetties along the Golok River were identified as entry points for undocumented migrants.
They include Pangkalan Haram Azizah, Parking, Pak Antah, MCA, Kuala Senggeng, Kedap and Perdah.
"The number shows that migrant smuggling syndicates do not rely on a single route but use several illegal jetties simultaneously to evade the authorities.
"When one landing point comes under tighter control, surveillance or a raid, the syndicates quickly switch to alternative routes, including hidden trails, plantations, village roads, Kasban roads and riverbanks," he said.
He said one of the main challenges in tackling migrant smuggling was the vast and complex border terrain, as well as the long and open stretch of the Golok River.
The presence of small rivers, forested areas, hidden trails and numerous illegal routes along the border also made surveillance difficult.
He added that hundreds of illegal jetties and alternative routes along the Kelantan border needed to be monitored by the authorities.
"Another challenge is the syndicates' constantly changing modus operandi. When one route comes under tighter control, they look for new ones, including sea routes and smaller rivers," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No question of Negri Sembilan assembly being dissolved, says MB
Article:
SEREMBAN: The Negri Sembilan state assembly will not be allowed to dissolve, and efforts will be made to ensure its sitting proceeds as scheduled, says Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim.
He said preparations for the tabling of the state Budget were finalised, with the state government now awaiting the official date for the sitting.
"Preparations for the Budget are all in place. We have also finalised it and are only waiting for the date to hold the state assembly sitting.
"We will do our best to ensure that it is held as scheduled. There is no question of the state assembly being dissolved.
"As the head of the state government, I will not allow the state assembly to be dissolved," he told reporters after attending a Deepavali open house hosted by special adviser on Indian community affairs Datuk VS Mogan.
He was responding to a question on the state government's preparations for the upcoming state assembly sitting.
The state government had previously planned to begin the sitting on Nov 26, followed by the tabling of the 2027 State Budget on Nov 27.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid cautions against further delays in implementing Najib's house arrest
Article:
ISTANBUL: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has cautioned against further delays in implementing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest.
He said the Attorney-General's Chambers is responsible for interpreting the law and constitutional provisions, and as such, there was no need to bring the matter back to court.
"There is no need for clarification from the courts as the implementation is based on a decision conclusively made by His Majesty the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
"In my view, the Pardons Board's decision must be fully complied with, as the Attorney-General (A-G) had issued a statement saying that once the RM50 million fine was paid, the board's directive and decision would automatically take effect," he told Malaysian media at the conclusion of his visit to Türkiye today.
Zahid said he respects the legal institutions and the Attorney-General's Chambers, but their credibility must be protected to maintain public confidence.
He welcomed the A-G's move to seek an audience with His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, over the issue.
"However, Istana Negara's statement was crystal clear on the King's powers under the Federal Constitution.
"His Majesty's prerogative as chairman of the Pardons Board should not be questioned."
On Friday, Umno confirmed that the RM50 million fine imposed on Najib had been
paid at the Kuala Lumpur High Court,
paving the way for the implementation of house arrest under the terms of his conditional pardon.
A-G Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar has also sought an audience with the King to explain his position on complying with the royal decree concerning Najib's Conditional Pardon Order.
Dusuki is also expected to explain the legal questions arising from the High Court's Release Order following payment of the RM50 million fine, which was a precondition for Najib's house arrest.
On Sept 18, the Federal Territories Pardons Board announced that the King had
consented to a conditional pardon
at the board's 64th meeting.
His Majesty consented to Najib serving the remainder of his six-year sentence under house arrest, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine for his SRC International case.
The board said Najib must comply with all conditions to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
Najib has been serving a reduced six-year prison sentence at Kajang Prison after the board halved his original 12-year sentence in February 2024.
The initial RM210 million fine was also reduced to RM50 million.
Najib is serving the sentence after the Federal Court upheld his conviction in the case on Aug 23, 2022.
He was found guilty of seven charges involving abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and money laundering over RM42 million belonging to SRC International, a former unit of 1Malaysia Development Bhd. He was sentenced to 12 years' jail and fined RM210 million.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sabah expected to table biggest-ever budget on Dec 4
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Sabah's 2027 Budget, scheduled to be tabled on Dec 4, is expected to be larger than this year's, says state Finance Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun.
He said the state government was still preparing the budget through consultation sessions, discussions and feedback from various quarters.
Masidi said the preparations must take into account the state's revenue and capacity to generate income.
Speaking to reporters at a Deepavali celebration at a hotel, he said that despite numerous requests for allocations, the government must remain practical and ensure spending did not exceed its financial capacity.
"What is important is that we continue to uphold sound financial management and good governance in preparing this budget," he said.
On development priorities, Masidi said the largest allocations each year were generally channelled towards the water supply and road sectors to address infrastructure problems faced by the people.
However, he said infrastructure projects took time to complete, and not all issues could be resolved within a short period.
Some projects initiated this year, he added, could take up to three years to complete.
He also urged consumers experiencing water supply problems to remain patient, saying the government was giving serious attention to the issue through substantial allocations.
Masidi said Sabah was awaiting the RM900 million special grant from the federal government.
"We have been told they are in the process of meeting all the accounting preconditions, so we hope it will be channelled this year," he said.
He said the additional allocation could potentially allow Sabah to table a budget approaching its maximum revenue capacity, estimated at nearly RM8 billion.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Khairy: Chinese voters not afraid of 'blue wave'
Article:
MELAKA: Cooperation between Barisan Nasional and Pas will not undermine the rights and interests of non-Malays, based on the two parties' experience of working together in the previous federal government.
Former Umno Youth chief Khairy Jamaluddin said he had never witnessed a situation in which BN component parties MCA and MIC felt uncomfortable with the presence or views of Pas ministers during cabinet meetings.
He said differences in political views were normal and could be managed harmoniously without threatening the interests of any community.
"I am a living witness who has worked with Pas at the federal level, and I had no problems.
"Pas has its views, MCA has its views, and Umno certainly has ours. But these differences never reached a point where the rights and interests of any community were threatened," he said in his speech at the Sembang Anak Muda programme in Kampung Batang Tiga, Bukit Rambai,
Khairy said BN's victories in several state constituencies with significant Chinese voter populations also showed that the community continued to support candidates from the coalition.
He cited MCA's previous electoral victories in Yong Peng through Ling Tian Soon, Chennah through Siow Kong Choon and Jementah through See Ann Giap as examples of Chinese voter support for BN.
He said the results showed that cooperation with Pas did not necessarily diminish BN's support among non-Malay voters.
"I came to campaign in Melaka because I do not want BN to win only Malay votes.
"We must win votes from Malays, Chinese, Indians and other communities," he said.
Khairy also expressed confidence that growing support for BN could translate into a "blue wave" at the ballot box, citing the encouraging reception he had received throughout his campaign tour.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Kota Laksamana could become new Melaka capital, say Ab Rauf
Article:
MELAKA: Kota Laksamana could become Melaka's new state capital under plans to develop a new economic corridor if Barisan Nasional  wins the seat in the Melaka election.
Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh said the proposal was part of the state government's plans to transform the area's development and economic landscape over the next five years.
He said Kota Laksamana's rapid development, particularly in the housing, tourism and medical sectors, had the potential to turn it into a new administrative centre for the state.
"I am targeting Kota Laksamana to become the state capital. That is what I hope for.
"Who can tell me where Melaka's capital is now? There is none. There is no such place.
"So, if we win Kota Laksamana, we will give its people a centre that will become the state capital of Melaka," he said at a campaign event for the Melaka election at the BN Kota Laksamana operations room here today.
Also present were MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong and BN candidate for Kota Laksamana, Melvin Chua Kew Wei.
Ab Rauf, who is also the caretaker Melaka chief minister, said the proposed economic corridor would include a medical hub, as well as various tourism and commercial projects expected to transform the state's economic landscape.
He said existing facilities and planned developments in the area included Encore Melaka, Oriental Melaka Straits Medical Centre and a new shopping mall in Klebang.
He said the plans would be implemented in stages, with the first five years serving as the foundation for further development.
"We will first take five years to draw up the initial plans, which can then be continued over the following five years," he said.
On the election contest, Ab Rauf said a BN victory in Kota Laksamana was not impossible, expressing confidence that Chua could spring a surprise in the polls.
"Our target is Kota Laksamana. I believe that this time, this year, this month, this term, it is not impossible for Melvin to become the people's representative.
"Given the times and circumstances, change is necessary. If we continue to remain where we are, it will be difficult to bring about change," he said.
Ab Rauf said the state government would help provide facilities and reduce bureaucracy to accelerate economic development in the area.
Melvin is facing a three-cornered contest against Pakatan Harapan candidate Low Chee Leong and Bersama candidate Ethan Lim Zhi Hao.
In the 2021 Melaka election, Low retained the seat with a majority of 11,494 votes.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Alliance Bank's BizSmart challenge down to 13 finalists
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 13 homegrown businesses have earned their place in the finals of Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd's BizSmart Challenge Accelerator Edition 2026.
The finalists come from a wide range of industries, including healthcare, children's therapy and education, personal care, home and living, digital media, food and beverage as well as retail.
Alliance Bank group chief executive officer Kellee Kam said the calibre of this year's finalists reflects the ambition, innovation and growing focus on sustainability among Malaysian entrepreneurs.
"Reaching the finals is no small feat, these founders have been tested on every aspect of their business, and they have risen to the challenge.
"Through the BizSmart Challenge, we connect promising businesses with the expertise, networks and financial solutions they need to scale sustainably and contribute to Malaysia's economic growth," he said in a statement.
The journey began with the 30 shortlisted contestants.
They completed a four-day Accelerator Programme and Business Coaching, led by subject-matter experts from Alliance Bank, Alliance Islamic Bank, 1337 Ventures, Cradle Fund, Sunway iLabs, Sunway Malls and OneCredit, the challenge's credit reporting partner.
The sessions covered credit readiness, business risk, halal certification and funding, sustainability and growth strategies. It also helped prepare the founders for the pitching rounds ahead.
Next, the contestants delivered a five-minute business pitch followed by a 10-minute question and answer session.
They then entered The Ultimate Elevator Pitch, where they had just 60 seconds to summarise their business proposition and make their case for a place in the finals.
This season's new Hot Seat Interrogation gave selected contestants a second chance to fight for a place in the finals.
The questions tested their business acumen, financial literacy, decision-making and crisis-management abilities.
Three contestants rose to the challenge and won Wild Card places in the finals.
Additionally, the new ESG Accelerator Award saw five shortlisted businesses pitch proposals showing how environmental, social and governance practices strengthen their operations and long-term profitability.
The 13 finalists will now compete for a total of RM400,000 in cash prizes for the top three placings, along with other special awards and opportunities supported by the challenge's partners.
These include the Partner Selection Award by Cradle, with a total of RM50,000 in cash prizes across three winners, the Investor Choice Award by 1337 Ventures and the FutureX Award by Sunway iLabs, as well as RM180,000 worth of media prizes from Seni Jaya.
The winners will be announced at the Awards Presentation Night on Nov 25.
Before then, the public can also have a say.
The 13 finalists will compete for the new People's Choice Award, which includes a RM10,000 cash prize sponsored by Alliance Bank for the finalist with the most votes.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Retiree loses RM179,490 in Macau scam
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 73-year-old retiree lost RM179,490 after falling victim to a Macau scam involving scammers posing as police officers and accusing him of money laundering and drug trafficking.
Brickfields police chief ACP Hoo Chang Hook said the victim was initially contacted by two unidentified individuals claiming to be police officers, who instructed him to surrender his bank cards, cash and jewellery for investigation purposes.
He said the victim, who panicked, later agreed to meet the suspects at an apartment in Sri Petaling on Sept 8 to hand over the money and valuables as instructed.
"The total losses amounted to RM179,490, involving cash handed over, gold purchases and transfers to three third-party bank accounts," he said when contacted today.
Hoo said the victim lodged a police report after realising he had been cheated.
Police were checking information with telecommunications companies and reviewing closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage to assist investigations under Section 420 of the Penal Code, he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Border security tightened in Kelantan amid migrant smuggling concerns
Article:
KOTA BARU: Border enforcement agencies have stepped up security in Kelantan amid concerns over a rise in undocumented migrants entering the state by sea and land routes.
An integrated operation involving several enforcement agencies, coordinated by the National Security Council (NSC) and led by the police, was launched on Nov 7 to tackle human trafficking, migrant smuggling and other cross-border criminal activities.
A source said the operation, which runs until Nov 20, also involved the Immigration Department and Marine police.
The operation is being conducted from 7pm to 7am, covering both maritime and land border areas.
"The operation reflects the seriousness of the authorities in addressing the growing threat of migrant smuggling and other cross-border crimes.
"All agencies are working together to strengthen enforcement and prevent syndicates from exploiting the state's coastal areas and land border routes," the source said.
Besides intensifying sea patrols to monitor suspicious movements along the coastline and waterways, enforcement agencies have increased roadblocks and inspections at strategic locations.
"The integrated approach is aimed at tightening security, disrupting smuggling networks and preventing undocumented migrants from entering the country through Kelantan," the source said.
The New Straits Times reported that
residents of 12 small islands
off the coast near here voiced concern over speedboats spotted in the area, which they believed were operated by human traffickers.
The boats were suspected of ferrying undocumented migrants from a neighbouring country into Kelantan, often under the cover of darkness.
Residents said the boats posed a risk to fishermen and villagers who frequently travelled between the islands, particularly those returning home from work at night.
They claimed the boat operators were foreigners familiar with landing points along the coast.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid brushes off talk of BN-PH rift over Najib house arrest issue
Article:
ISTANBUL: Barisan Nasional (BN) has dismissed claims that the issue surrounding the conditional pardon and house arrest for Datuk Seri Najib Razak has caused a rift with Pakatan Harapan (PH).
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said coalitions continue to work professionally despite differing views, adding that Malaysia's political maturity was at an almost optimum level.
"There is no problem between us. We run our ministries and sit in Cabinet every week, and the work of government is carried out professionally.
"There have been no differences of opinion, let alone disputes, in more than four years.
"The professionalism we practise is based not only on official duties, but also on other tasks that we carry out," he told Malaysian media here.
Zahid was asked whether the issue surrounding Najib's conditional pardon and house arrest could further strain BN–PH ties in the unity government.
Zahid, who is also Deputy Prime Minister, acknowledged that differences in views and party positions existed, but said these were managed as best as possible.
He said differences at the state level, particularly in Johor, Negeri Sembilan and Melaka, had not affected BN-PH cooperation at the federal level.
"In my view, despite the different political moves, it will not affect the political stability of our country," he said.
Asked about calls for BN to withdraw support for Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Zahid said the issue did not arise as the recent Umno General Assembly resolution had decided that BN would remain in the unity government until the end of the term.
However, he said when the term would end was up to the prime minister, as head of the 15th Parliament, and the political situation at the time.
"When that time comes, we will, of course, go our separate political ways.
"But it is not impossible that after the election, a formula and political steps will need to be negotiated and finalised later," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain forecast in 11 states, three Federal Territories until 6pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are forecast to hit 11 states and all three Federal Territories until 6pm today.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said the adverse weather is expected across the whole of Penang, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan and Melaka, as well as the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and Labuan.
In Kedah, the affected areas are Kulim, Bandar Baharu and Baling, while in Perak, the warning covers Bagan Datuk, Hilir Perak, Perak Tengah, Manjung, Kinta, Kampar, Kuala Kangsar, Larut Matang, Kerian, Selama, Batang Padang and Muallim.
In Kelantan, the warning covers Kuala Krai, Jeli and Gua Musang, while in Pahang, it involves Temerloh, Lipis, Rompin, Bera, Maran, Kuantan, Jerantut and Pekan.
In Johor, the affected areas are Muar, Tangkak and Segamat.
Meanwhile, in Sarawak, bad weather is forecast for Mukah (Dalat, Matu, Daro and Tanjung Manis), Sibu (Sibu), Bintulu (Tatau), Sri Aman (Pantu, Lingga and Sri Aman), Limbang, Miri (Marudi and Bario), Sarikei (Maradong), Kapit (Kapit) and Betong (Pusa and Betong).
In Sabah, the warning covers Kudat, Sandakan (Paitan, Telupid and Tongod), the West Coast, the Interior, and Tawau (Semporna, Tawau, Lahad Datu and Kunak).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid's Turkiye visit advances US$10b trade ambition, defence and education cooperation
Article:
ISTANBUL: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has concluded his four-day working visit to Turkiye, with engagements focused on strengthening Malaysia-Turkiye ties in trade, defence, education and diplomacy.
The Nov 5-8 visit aimed to sustain momentum in high-level exchanges between the two countries, which have maintained diplomatic relations since June 17, 1964.
It also sought to build on ties elevated to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in 2022.
Zahid, who is also rural and regional development minister, began his visit by attending the 2026 TRT World Forum at the Istanbul Congress Centre on Nov 6, at the invitation of the Turkish Radio and Television Corporation (TRT).
He participated in a panel discussion titled "Turkiye: From Regional Power to Multi-Regional Actor".
He later met Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, with both sides discussing plans to increase bilateral trade from US$5.6 billion in 2025 to US$10 billion by 2030.
They also exchanged views on Palestine, Lebanon and Syria, emphasising the protection of civilians, humanitarian access and diplomatic solutions.
Discussions also covered wider cooperation in investment, defence, technology transfer, technical and vocational education and training, halal development and disaster management, with the High-Level Strategic Cooperation Council serving as the coordinating mechanism.
Zahid also reaffirmed Malaysia's commitment to its role as Asean-Turkiye relations coordinator.
He also met Turkish Vice-President Cevdet Yilmaz, with discussions focusing on investment opportunities in food and beverage, semiconductors, artificial intelligence, electrical and electronics, and defence.
Both sides agreed to work towards a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on defence cooperation.
Malaysia's military procurement from Turkiye since 2000 is estimated at US$3.4 billion.
On the sidelines of the visit, Zahid met D-8 Secretary-General Sohail Mahmood, who said intra-trade among member countries stood at about US$170 billion, against a target of US$500 billion by 2030.
The D-8 welcomed Malaysia's proposal to expand halal cooperation, including in Islamic finance, pharmaceuticals and vaccines, and expressed readiness to review the proposal to establish an International Zakat Organisation.
On defence and maritime cooperation, Zahid and Malaysia's honorary consul in Bursa, Datuk Cevdet Sefer, explored the potential of establishing a ship maintenance, repair and overhaul hub in Bagan Datuk.
He also met Lebanese Deputy Prime Minister Dr Tarek Mitri, who expressed appreciation for the contributions of Malaysian peacekeepers serving under the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon.
On education, Zahid met Turkiye's Higher Education Council president Prof Dr Erol Ozvar, with both sides identifying joint PhD programmes, quantum technology and semiconductors as immediate priorities.
Turkiye will prepare draft proposals covering the three areas.
Letters of Collaboration were also exchanged involving Universiti Kuala Lumpur, Universiti Poly-Tech Malaysia, Sabanci University and Yildiz Technical University.
A reciprocal visit by experts has been proposed for the first quarter of 2027.
Zahid also held a high-level policy dialogue with Turkish think tank Foundation for Political, Economic and Social Research (Seta), where both sides agreed to continue strategic dialogue and expand cooperation in policy research.
Seta shared its analysis on Syria, Palestine, United States foreign policy and maritime security, which did not constitute any new Malaysian policy commitment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: New Covid-19 strain PJ.2.1 may mimic cold or flu symptoms – WHO
Article:
MOSCOW: Symptoms of the new Covid-19 strain PJ.2.1 may be similar to those of a cold or flu, and testing is necessary, the World Health Organisation (WHO) said, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti.
"Symptoms of Covid-19, influenza and other respiratory infections can overlap. Therefore, based on symptoms alone, it is impossible to determine with certainty which respiratory virus caused the infection," the WHO said.
Testing may be required in cases where establishing the cause of the illness could affect treatment decisions or public health decision-making, the organisation noted.
The WHO's Russian office earlier said that the risk of the new coronavirus strain PJ.2.1 spreading globally was increasing.
The WHO also noted that it was closely monitoring the spread of the new strain.
On Saturday, Doctor of Medical Sciences, infectious disease specialist and virologist Elena Malinnikova said that a severe sore throat and a longer period of fatigue following illness could distinguish the new coronavirus strain PJ.2.1 from other variants.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Crew member missing as Indonesian water-bombing helicopter crashes [WATCH]
Article:
JAKARTA: A helicopter battling Indonesian wildfires crashed into a river on Sunday while scooping up water, an official told AFP, with two crew members rescued and one still missing.
The crash in Borneo's South Kalimantan province was the second in days involving a firefighting helicopter, after a military chopper plunged into waters off Borneo on Wednesday, killing three people.
Two Australian nationals survived Sunday's incident and were "safe", said Berton Panjaitan, a spokesman for the National Disaster Mitigation Agency, while the third crew member, an Indonesian, remained unaccounted for.
Dramatic video footage showed the firefighting helicopter being slowly dragged downwards after filling its bucket from the Barito River, eventually plunging nose-first into the water.
The Southeast Asian archipelago has for months been struggling to control blazes that have burned through large swathes of Sumatra, Borneo and Papua, causing choking haze that drifted to neighbouring Malaysia, Timor-Leste and Singapore.
"This incident occurred while the air fleet was conducting a water-bombing operation," spokesman Berton said of Sunday's crash.
"In footage captured by an amateur video, the helicopter appears to lose control while manoeuvring after scooping up water from the river with a Bambi Bucket."
The Eurocopter EC225LP Super Puma belonged to a company the disaster mitigation agency had contracted for water-bombing operations, he added.
On Wednesday, a helicopter carrying eight people crashed during a mission to fight fires in Tanjung Puting National Park, home to animals including critically endangered Bornean orangutans.
The incident occurred while the aircraft was scooping seawater for water-bombing, according to an army statement, which added that the cause of the accident was under investigation.
Aside from ground-based firefighters, Indonesia has relied heavily on air operations to fight the fires, which have destroyed more than 1.9 million hectares, according to deforestation monitor Nusantara Atlas.
The fires are driven in part by a strong El Nino weather phenomenon, which typically causes drought in Indonesia.
